text:
Alex: heads-up — console dashboards that join route_metadata -> metrics_raw are blowing up for big tenants, queries time out and UI shows partial results :grimacing:
Marta: saw that at 02:10 UTC, reproduced on staging with synthetic 60k routes. Indexes help a bit but join fanout still kills p99 CPU.
Sam: can you paste the slow query / explain?
Alex: here’s the simplified one we run from dashboard service:
```sql
SELECT r.route_id, r.tenant_id, m.timestamp, m.qps
FROM route_metadata r
JOIN metrics_raw m ON m.route_id = r.route_id
WHERE r.tenant_id = $1 AND m.timestamp >= $2
ORDER BY m.timestamp DESC
LIMIT 1000;
```
Alex: explain shows nested loop + seq scan on metrics_raw on high-card tenants.
Harper: main problem is metrics_raw is sharded by time and has tag arrays, route_metadata is denormalized across several joins. We keep doing route lookups per metric row.
Marta: options: 1) materialized view per-tenant pre-joined time-windowed shard, 2) denormalize route_identity (tenant+alias) into metrics_raw at ingest, 3) precompute per-route timeseries rollups.
Sam: (1) avoids changing ingest pipeline but MV size is big; backfill could be heavy. (2) changes ingest hot path but small storage cost; seems simpler for reads. (3) good for aggregated dashboards but loses raw events.
Alex: propose we try a compact "route_identity" column on metrics_raw (text) filled at ingest + a tiny index on (route_identity, timestamp DESC) to accelerate the dashboard join without changing existing queries. Backfill plan for historical data via a batch job.
Marta: +1. Can we make route_identity a hashed short id (eg `tenant_shash || ':' || route_alias`) so indexes stay small?
Harper: hashed key works. Need migration plan: add nullable column, deploy ingest change to write new rows with route_identity, run streaming backfill for existing rows (non-blocking), then switch dashboard query to use route_identity and drop join.
Sam: sketch of migration SQL:
```sql
ALTER TABLE metrics_raw ADD COLUMN route_identity text;
UPDATE metrics_raw SET route_identity = tenant_id || ':' || route_alias WHERE route_identity IS NULL AND timestamp < now() - interval '7 days'; -- batch older
-- streaming task fills newest rows as they arrive via the ingest worker
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_metrics_routeid_time ON metrics_raw (route_identity, timestamp DESC);
```
Sam: do everything CONCURRENTLY where possible. Run batch in small windows to avoid IO spikes.
Alex: infra-bot created task https://redwood.internal/tasks/ANALYTICS-472 — contains backfill workers and failure alerts.
infra-bot: deployment note: feature-flagging ingest change recommended. Use `metrics.route_identity` flag scoped by cluster.
Marta: can ops tolerate the temporary 10-15% extra disk for duplicates? storage estimate ~+12% for top tenants.
Harper: yes, we have buffer. We should also add a safety TTL for route_identity backfill jobs and throttling by tenant.
Alex: action items: @Marta to own migration rollout & runbook, @Sam to land ingest change + flag, @Harper to implement streaming backfill workers. Blockers?
Marta: will draft runbook (backfill windows, rollback, observability queries) and post in #incidents if we hit errors.
Sam: will open PR with feature flag and test harness. CC @harper for integration.
Harper: will prototype backfill workers tomorrow; will add metrics for per-tenant progress.
Alex: timeline proposal: land ingest change behind flag in next 48h, start conservative backfill next weekend (low traffic), switch dashboard queries after 95% backfill per-tenant.
Marta: sounds good. One more: we should update console docs to show the new index and fallback join for older tenants.
Sam: noted. I’ll add a console migration page under docs/internal/analytics-migrations.
Alex: thanks — will follow up with the task progress later. :thumbsup:
